action: DO: Keep the first move small, private, and reversible
avoid: DON'T: Demand emotional disclosure as the entry price ('Yuk tumpahkan semuanya')
rationale: Lowering response cost (M01) matters far more than raising emotional intensity. Men avoid exposure, not help.
boundaryCondition: Acute suicide crisis requires unambiguous instruction, not low-pressure hedging.

doExamples.example: Sesi berikutnya Selasa, 19.00. Boleh datang, boleh cuma lihat-lihat dulu.
doExamples.why: Two options offered at once, so arriving is not a commitment to anything.

doExamples.example: Nggak perlu daftar. Datang aja, dan boleh pulang kapan saja.
doExamples.why: Removes both the entry step and the exit cost in one line.

doExamples.example: Balas dengan satu kata kalau mau infonya. Kalau nggak, pesan ini nggak perlu dibalas.
doExamples.why: Makes not responding an explicitly acceptable outcome rather than a silence he has to justify.

doExamples.example: Minggu lalu yang datang tujuh orang. Dua di antaranya nggak ngomong sama sekali.
doExamples.why: Describes the room with a verifiable detail, which does the work that a promise of safety cannot.

dontExamples.example: Yuk tumpahin semua unek-unekmu di sini!
dontExamples.why: Disclosure as the stated purpose of arriving is the entry price this rule exists to remove.

dontExamples.example: Ceritakan pengalaman tersulitmu di kolom komentar.
dontExamples.why: Asks for the highest-exposure act available on a public surface.

dontExamples.example: Isi form ini dulu ya, biar kami tahu kondisi kamu.
dontExamples.why: Puts an assessment in front of the door, so the cost is paid before anything is received.

dontExamples.example: Konfirmasi kehadiran dengan komen ‘HADIR’.
dontExamples.why: Turns attendance into a public declaration in front of everyone who can see the thread.

action: DO: Use concrete situations to let emotion arrive naturally ('Jam tiga pagi, masih ngecek saldo')
avoid: DON'T: Lead with diagnostic labels or clinical jargon ('Kamu mungkin depresi')
rationale: Men prefer coded emotional language and direct behavioral language simultaneously (Sharp et al.). Everyday detail earns the feeling.
boundaryCondition: High-risk safety protocols require clinical precision and direct terminology.

doExamples.example: Jam tiga pagi, masih ngecek saldo.
doExamples.why: One observable situation, no feeling named, nothing for him to concede.

doExamples.example: Motor udah dipanasin, tapi belum berangkat-berangkat juga.
doExamples.why: A physical detail that carries the state without diagnosing it.

doExamples.example: Chat dari bos kebaca jam sebelas malam. Dibalas jam sebelas lewat dua.
doExamples.why: Two timestamps do the work an adjective would have done badly.

doExamples.example: Makan siang tetap jalan. Cuma sekarang sambil buka aplikasi lowongan.
doExamples.why: Functioning and not being fine shown in the same sentence, which is the recognition this rule is for.

dontExamples.example: Kamu mungkin depresi.
dontExamples.why: A diagnostic label aimed at the reader before he has agreed to be a reader.

dontExamples.example: Ini gejala anxiety disorder yang harus kamu waspadai.
dontExamples.why: Clinical terminology arriving before any everyday description, which reverses the sequencing rule.

dontExamples.example: Apakah kamu merasa hampa dan kehilangan makna hidup?
dontExamples.why: An open introspective question that costs him something to answer.

dontExamples.example: 5 Tanda Kamu Butuh Bantuan Profesional.
dontExamples.why: Puts the conclusion in the headline, at the point of highest exposure.

action: DO: Use 'kamu' as default institutional address; reserve 'gue/lo' strictly for named peer creators
avoid: DON'T: Use corporate 'gue/lo' or forced 'bro' from an anonymous institutional account
rationale: Relatability is relationally licensed (M09). Institutional slang is universally diagnosed as cringe impersonation.
boundaryCondition: Individual staff writing personal reflections may authentically use their natural dialect.

doExamples.example: Kamu boleh cerita, boleh juga cuma dengerin.
doExamples.why: Kamu as the institutional default: direct without claiming intimacy.

doExamples.example: Kami di Menungsa nyediain ruangnya. Kami nggak nanya kalau kamu belum mau cerita.
doExamples.why: Kami keeps the organisation honest about being an organisation rather than a friend.

doExamples.example: Gue Rio, tim konten Menungsa. Gue yang nulis ini.
doExamples.why: Gue is licensed here because a named person is speaking as himself.

doExamples.example: Nomor ini dipegang Dimas. Kalau dia lagi nggak online, balasannya besok pagi.
doExamples.why: Attribution plus an honest limit on availability, which is what makes the informal register credible.

dontExamples.example: Bro, lo nggak sendirian kok!
dontExamples.why: Vernacular from an unattributed account is a credibility event, not a stylistic choice.

dontExamples.example: Gaes, yuk jaga mental health kalian!
dontExamples.why: Borrowed peer register plus borrowed English, from a speaker with no licence for either.

dontExamples.example: Kita semua pasti pernah down, kan?
dontExamples.why: Kita asserted before there is a we, which reads as presumption rather than solidarity.

dontExamples.example: Halo Sobat Menungsa!
dontExamples.why: A manufactured in-group name assigns him a membership he never agreed to.

action: DO: Use gender cues only when an action is already culturally feminine-coded and publicly observed
avoid: DON'T: Brand neutral actions as 'for real men' or 'pria sejati'
rationale: Where no gender conflict exists, adding gender manufactures an identity threat and triggers reactance.
boundaryCondition: Skincare or vulnerability in public view can benefit from masculine identity reassurance.

doExamples.example: Panduan menjaga kesehatan mental sehari-hari.
doExamples.why: Gender-unmarked default, which is where the evidence sits for most content.

doExamples.example: Layanan konseling khusus laki-laki dewasa.
doExamples.why: Descriptive demographic marking: it says who the service is for without claiming what a man is.

doExamples.example: Ruang ini isinya laki-laki semua. Itu aja bedanya.
doExamples.why: States the fact and then closes the subject, refusing the invitation to define masculinity.

dontExamples.example: Pria sejati nggak takut cerita.
dontExamples.why: Defines manhood conditionally and then makes the reader buy it back.

dontExamples.example: Buktikan kamu cukup kuat buat hadapi ini.
dontExamples.why: A challenge frame, which is the configuration with the clearest documented backfire.

dontExamples.example: Sebagai laki-laki, kamu harus mau lebih terbuka.
dontExamples.why: Prescriptive gender injunction: the construction that produced measurable reactance.

dontExamples.example: Cowok banget nggak sih kalau nangis?
dontExamples.why: Puts his masculinity on trial in the middle of the sentence that was meant to help.

action: DO: Design around household and relational care channels (e.g. supporting wives, friends, peers)
avoid: DON'T: Assume the solo, autonomous, self-advocating individual help-seeker model from Western frameworks
rationale: Indonesian care is relational; households organize care through division of labor; community supplies both care and surveillance.
mechanism: M11 Relational Care & M12 Community Surveillance
boundaryCondition: Unmarried or alienated urban youth without family support require alternative peer networks.

doExamples.example: Kalau kamu istri, ibu, atau teman dekat yang lagi khawatir: ini yang bisa kamu lakukan duluan.
doExamples.why: Addresses the person who actually arranges care in the Indonesian household.

doExamples.example: Boleh datang berdua. Banyak yang gitu.
doExamples.why: Permits the relational route and normalises it in four words.

doExamples.example: Kalau kamu nggak sanggup nelpon sendiri, minta orang terdekat yang nelpon.
doExamples.why: Accounts for someone unable to act alone, which is the relational finding at its most consequential.

doExamples.example: Biaya ditanggung JKN. Kartunya bisa dipakai satu keluarga.
doExamples.why: Treats the household as the unit that pays, because it usually is.

dontExamples.example: Kesehatan mentalmu tanggung jawabmu sendiri.
dontExamples.why: Imports the autonomous help-seeker model that the Indonesian evidence does not support.

dontExamples.example: Cuma kamu yang bisa nolong diri kamu.
dontExamples.why: Closes off the route that most Indonesian men actually use.

dontExamples.example: Jangan bergantung sama orang lain, mulai dari diri sendiri.
dontExamples.why: Reframes ordinary relational care as a personal weakness.

dontExamples.example: Ambil kendali penuh atas hidupmu.
dontExamples.why: Assigns full control to someone whose main barriers are institutional and material.

action: DO: Keep moral concentration low and back claims with concrete, costly institutional commitments
avoid: DON'T: Preach, scold, or position the reader/men collectively as culprits
rationale: Moral density above saturation triggers reactance and cynical virtue-discounting (M10, M18).
mechanism: M10 Motive Attribution & M18 Moral Saturation
boundaryCondition: Legitimate institutional advocacy can state clear ethical boundaries without berating the audience.

doExamples.example: Antrean psikiater di puskesmas rata-rata dua minggu. Kami lagi mendata mana yang lebih cepat, dan datanya kami buka.
doExamples.why: Structural subject, plus a commitment that costs something to keep.

doExamples.example: Kami nolak iklan suplemen di kanal ini. Artinya kami kehilangan pemasukan.
doExamples.why: One moral position, stated once, with its price made visible.

doExamples.example: Jam layanan puskesmas selesai jam satu siang. Buat yang kerja shift, itu masalah nyata.
doExamples.why: Names the barrier without naming a culprit, which is the distinction this rule protects.

doExamples.example: Konten itu salah kami. Sudah kami turunkan, dan ini alasannya.
doExamples.why: Moral seriousness aimed at the organisation's own conduct rather than at the audience.

dontExamples.example: Laki-laki Indonesia harus berhenti gengsi.
dontExamples.why: Personal subject and a collective indictment in one sentence.

dontExamples.example: Sudah saatnya kita semua peduli kesehatan mental!
dontExamples.why: Moral scolding with no cost attached and kita with no real referent.

dontExamples.example: Stop normalisasi budaya toxic masculinity sekarang juga!
dontExamples.why: Maximises moral density, which is the region where persuasion collapses even as sharing rises.

dontExamples.example: Kalau kamu masih diam, kamu bagian dari masalahnya.
dontExamples.why: Converts the reader into the culprit, which is the reactance configuration in its purest form.

action: DO: Evaluate programs by actual conversion, help-seeking behavior, and comment valence
avoid: DON'T: Use likes, shares, or viral reach as proxies for trust or persuasion
rationale: Engagement conflates approval with outrage and algorithmic feedback. Outrage spreads fast but depresses real action.
boundaryCondition: Top-of-funnel brand awareness can track reach if isolated from conversion goals.

doExamples.example: Bulan ini: 34 orang buka halaman puskesmas, 9 klik nomor, 4 datang.
doExamples.why: Counts the costly acts, in the order they have to happen.

doExamples.example: Komentar yang nanya lokasi: 12. Yang isinya marah: 2.
doExamples.why: Separates comment valence rather than reporting comments as one number.

doExamples.example: Dari lima sesi, rata-rata tujuh orang datang. Dua orang datang lebih dari sekali.
doExamples.why: Return attendance is the closest available proxy for the thing the programme is for.

dontExamples.example: Jangkauan bulan ini 240.000, naik 300%.
dontExamples.why: Reach is the metric the outrage findings warn about most directly.

dontExamples.example: Konten ini viral, artinya pesannya nyampe.
dontExamples.why: Treats diffusion as evidence of conversion, which the petition data contradicts.

dontExamples.example: Engagement rate kita tertinggi se-kategori.
dontExamples.why: Optimises the number that rises fastest when a message is doing the wrong thing.
